questions.q: Do Earth's magnetic poles ever swap places?
choices: Yes, many times in the past
questions.fact: Rocks on the sea floor record these flips like a striped barcode.

questions.q: What is the name for the outer rigid shell of Earth made of the crust and upper mantle?
questions.fact: The lithosphere is broken into the tectonic plates.

questions.q: What is the name for all of Earth's water, including oceans, lakes and ice?
questions.fact: Hydro comes from the Greek word for water.

questions.q: What is the name for all the living things on Earth together?
questions.fact: The biosphere reaches from deep underground to high in the sky.

questions.q: What gives Earth's sky its colors during sunrise and sunset?
questions.fact: Dust and pollution can make sunsets even more colorful.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to spin once on its axis?
questions.fact: Earth actually spins once every 23 hours and 56 minutes compared with the stars.

questions.q: About how fast does a point on the equator move as Earth spins?
questions.fact: We do not feel it because everything around us moves along with us.

questions.q: What shape is Earth?
choices: A sphere that bulges a little at the equator
questions.fact: Earth's spin makes it about 43 kilometers wider around the equator than from pole to pole.

questions.q: About how far is it around Earth at the equator?
questions.fact: An ancient Greek scientist named Eratosthenes estimated it closely more than 2,000 years ago.

questions.q: Which ancient Greek scientist measured Earth's size using shadows and wells?
questions.fact: He compared shadows in two Egyptian cities to calculate Earth's circumference.

questions.q: Why do we have leap years?
choices: To give February more days for fun
Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to orbit the Sun
questions.fact: Adding a day every four years keeps the calendar matched with the seasons.

questions.q: When it is summer in the United States, what season is it in Australia?
questions.fact: The Northern and Southern Hemispheres have opposite seasons.

questions.q: What do we call the season between summer and winter?
questions.fact: Autumn is also called fall in the United States because leaves fall from trees.

questions.q: Why do leaves change color in autumn?
choices: Green chlorophyll breaks down and other colors show
questions.fact: Shorter days and cooler nights tell trees to stop making chlorophyll.

questions.q: Why do some places near the equator have only wet and dry seasons?
choices: They get strong sunlight all year
questions.fact: Near the equator, temperatures stay warm, so rain is what changes most.

questions.q: What is the gemstone form of the mineral corundum that is red?
questions.fact: Blue corundum is called sapphire.

questions.q: What is a blue gemstone made of the mineral corundum?
questions.fact: Sapphires can also be pink, yellow and many other colors.

questions.q: What is a green gemstone that is a type of the mineral beryl?
questions.fact: Most emeralds have tiny flaws inside, which jewelers call the garden.

questions.q: What is a purple gemstone made of quartz?
questions.fact: The name comes from a Greek word, because people once believed it stopped drunkenness.

questions.q: Which gemstone forms inside oysters instead of in the ground?
questions.fact: Pearls are one of the few gems made by living animals.

questions.q: How do diamonds usually reach Earth's surface?
choices: Carried up by deep volcanic eruptions
questions.fact: Most diamonds formed more than 150 kilometers underground over a billion years ago.

questions.q: What is the largest gem-quality diamond ever found?
questions.fact: It was found in South Africa in 1905 and cut into stones for the British Crown Jewels.

questions.q: Which famous blue diamond is in the Smithsonian museum and rumored to be cursed?
questions.fact: The Hope Diamond glows red-orange for a while after being exposed to ultraviolet light.

questions.q: What is an ore?
choices: Rock containing enough metal to be worth mining
questions.fact: Iron ore is melted in furnaces to make iron and steel.

questions.q: Which metal ore is the main source of aluminum?
questions.fact: Australia is one of the world's biggest producers of bauxite.

questions.q: Which mineral, used for rock salt, is mined from the ground?
questions.fact: Halite is the mineral name for table salt.

questions.q: Which soft mineral is used to make plaster and drywall?
questions.fact: A cave in Mexico called the Cave of the Crystals has gypsum crystals longer than a bus.

questions.q: Which flaky mineral splits into thin, see-through sheets?
questions.fact: Mica was once used for windows in stoves and lanterns.

questions.q: What lies under Yellowstone National Park?
questions.fact: Yellowstone sits on top of a huge hot spot of magma deep underground.

questions.q: What are hot spots in Earth's mantle known for creating?
choices: Chains of volcanic islands like Hawaii
questions.fact: As the plate moves over the hot spot, new islands form in a line.

questions.q: Which Hawaiian volcano has been one of the most active in the world?
questions.fact: In Hawaiian tradition, Kilauea is home to Pele, the goddess of fire and volcanoes.

questions.q: What is the name for volcanic rock fragments that fly through the air during an eruption?
questions.fact: Tephra includes everything from fine ash to huge volcanic bombs.

questions.q: What is a fast, deadly cloud of hot gas and rock that rushes down a volcano called?
questions.fact: Pyroclastic flows can move faster than 100 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: What are volcanic mudflows called?
questions.fact: Lahars form when volcanic ash mixes with water from rain or melting snow.

questions.q: Which island country formed on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge has many volcanoes and geysers?
questions.fact: In Iceland, you can stand where the North American and Eurasian plates are pulling apart.

questions.q: Which new island formed from an undersea volcano near Iceland in 1963?
questions.fact: Scientists have studied Surtsey to see how plants and animals arrive on brand-new land.

questions.q: Which Japanese mountain is a famous volcano?
questions.fact: Mount Fuji last erupted in 1707.

questions.q: Which Philippine volcano's 1991 eruption cooled the whole planet for about a year?
questions.fact: It threw so much gas into the stratosphere that global temperatures dropped about half a degree Celsius.

questions.q: Which large lake in Central Asia has mostly dried up because its rivers were used to water crops?
questions.fact: The Aral Sea was once one of the four largest lakes in the world.

questions.q: Which sea has no coastline at all?
questions.fact: The Sargasso Sea in the Atlantic is defined by ocean currents and floating seaweed.

questions.q: What is a strait?
choices: A narrow channel of water connecting two larger bodies of water
questions.fact: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe from Africa.

questions.q: What is a lagoon?
choices: Shallow water separated from the sea by a reef or sandbar
questions.fact: Venice, Italy, was built on islands in a lagoon.

questions.q: What are the steep rocky walls along a coast, worn by waves, called?
questions.fact: Waves can carve sea cliffs into arches and tall stacks of rock.

questions.q: What is a natural rock arch along a coast eventually likely to become?
questions.fact: When the top of the arch collapses, the pillar left standing is called a stack.

questions.q: What are most beaches made of?
questions.fact: Some Hawaiian beaches have black sand made from volcanic rock.

questions.q: What is the pink sand on some beaches in Bermuda partly made of?
choices: Tiny red shells of sea creatures
questions.fact: The tiny creatures are called foraminifera.

questions.q: What do you call a large, slow-moving swirl of ocean currents?
questions.fact: Garbage patches form in the middle of gyres.

questions.q: What is a powerful swirling body of water, like in some narrow sea passages, called?
questions.fact: The Saltstraumen in Norway is one of the strongest tidal currents in the world.

questions.q: What is a rip current?
choices: A strong current pulling water away from the beach
questions.fact: If caught in one, swim parallel to the shore until you are out of it.

questions.q: How deep can sunlight reach in the ocean?
questions.fact: Below 1,000 meters, it is completely dark.

questions.q: How much of the ocean have people mapped in high detail, as of 2025?
questions.fact: As of 2025, about a quarter of the sea floor has been mapped in high detail.

questions.q: What color does deep, clear ocean water look, and why?
choices: Blue, because water absorbs red light
questions.fact: Water absorbs red, orange and yellow light, leaving mostly blue.

questions.q: What makes some lakes look bright turquoise?
questions.fact: This fine dust is called rock flour.

questions.q: What is the place where a river's fresh water mixes with the sea's salt water called?
questions.fact: Estuaries are rich nurseries for young fish.

questions.q: What is a curving bend in a river called?
questions.fact: When a meander gets cut off, it can become an oxbow lake.

questions.q: What is the flat land beside a river that floods sometimes called?
questions.fact: Floodplains have very rich soil because floods leave behind mud.

questions.q: What is a lake made by people when they build a dam called?
questions.fact: Many cities get their drinking water from reservoirs.

questions.q: Which river flows through Egypt and helped ancient Egyptians farm?
questions.fact: Its yearly floods left fertile mud along the riverbanks.

questions.q: Which river is the longest in the United States?
questions.fact: The Missouri is slightly longer than the Mississippi, which it flows into.

questions.q: What is the largest canyon in the world by some measures, in Tibet?
questions.fact: It is deeper than the Grand Canyon in Arizona.

questions.q: What is the giant red sandstone rock in the middle of Australia, sacred to Aboriginal people, called?
questions.fact: Uluru seems to change color, glowing bright red at sunrise and sunset.

questions.q: What is the huge crack in East Africa where the continent is slowly splitting apart called?
questions.fact: In millions of years, eastern Africa may break off to form a new landmass.

questions.q: Which large mountain range separates Europe and Asia?
questions.fact: The Ural Mountains are very old and have been worn down by erosion.

questions.q: Which mountain range in Europe includes Mont Blanc?
questions.fact: Mont Blanc is the tallest mountain in the Alps.

questions.q: How much of the Sahara is covered by sand dunes?
questions.fact: Most of the Sahara is rocky plains and gravel.

questions.q: Was the Sahara Desert always a desert?
choices: No, it was green with lakes thousands of years ago
It used to be an ocean last century
It used to be covered in ice last century
questions.fact: Ancient rock art in the Sahara shows giraffes and hippos.

questions.q: What is the large region of Earth near the equator that is warm all year called?
questions.fact: The tropics lie between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.q: What do we call the climate zones between the tropics and the polar regions, with four seasons?
questions.fact: Most of the United States and Europe are in the temperate zone.

questions.q: What is the climate of most rainforests?
choices: Dry for half the year with snow
questions.fact: Some rainforests get more than 2.5 meters of rain a year.

questions.q: What kind of climate does the Mediterranean region have?
choices: Hot dry summers and mild wet winters
questions.fact: California, parts of Chile and South Africa have Mediterranean climates too.

questions.q: Why are mountaintops colder than valleys?
choices: They are closer to space ice
Air gets thinner and cooler higher up
questions.fact: Temperatures often drop about 6.5 degrees Celsius for every kilometer you climb.

questions.q: Why are places near the ocean often milder than places far inland?
choices: The ocean makes its own heat
questions.fact: This is why coastal cities usually have cooler summers and warmer winters.

questions.q: What is a heat wave?
choices: Several days of unusually hot weather
A wave in a hot tub
questions.fact: Drinking water and staying in shade help people stay safe in a heat wave.

questions.q: What is El Niño?
choices: A warming of the Pacific Ocean that changes weather around the world
questions.fact: El Niño means the boy in Spanish, because fishermen noticed it around Christmas.

questions.q: What is the cooling of the Pacific Ocean, opposite to El Niño, called?
questions.fact: La Niña means the girl in Spanish.

questions.q: What does a weather forecast use to predict the weather?
choices: Data from satellites, radar and weather stations
questions.fact: Supercomputers run weather models millions of times faster than people could.

questions.q: What does weather radar mainly detect?
choices: Rain, snow and hail in clouds
questions.fact: Radar sends out radio waves that bounce off raindrops and come back.

questions.q: What is a cold front?
choices: The edge of a cold air mass pushing into warmer air
questions.fact: Cold fronts often bring thunderstorms and then cooler, clearer weather.

questions.q: What weather does high air pressure usually bring?
questions.fact: Low pressure often brings clouds, wind and rain.

questions.q: What is the windiest continent on Earth?
questions.fact: Winds pouring down off the Antarctic ice can be stronger than hurricane winds.

questions.q: How thick is the ice in Antarctica at its thickest?
questions.fact: The ice sheet is so heavy it pushes the land beneath it down.

questions.q: What is a huge floating shelf of ice attached to the coast of Antarctica called?
questions.fact: The Ross Ice Shelf is about the size of France.

questions.q: What is the name of the largest lake buried under the Antarctic ice?
questions.fact: Lake Vostok is under about 4 kilometers of ice and has been sealed off for millions of years.

questions.q: Which is the coldest place inhabited all year by people, a village in Siberia?
questions.fact: Winter temperatures in Oymyakon can fall below minus 60 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What does a compass point to on Earth?
questions.fact: Magnetic north is not exactly the same spot as the geographic North Pole, and it slowly moves.

questions.q: Is magnetic north moving?
choices: Yes, it has been drifting toward Siberia
It moves to the equator each summer
questions.fact: Scientists update maps of magnetic north every few years because of this drift.

questions.q: What are topographic maps used to show?
choices: The shape and height of the land
questions.fact: Contour lines that are close together show steep slopes.

questions.q: What does a map scale tell you?
choices: How distances on the map compare to real distances
questions.fact: For example, 1 centimeter on the map might equal 1 kilometer in real life.

questions.q: What is the science of making maps called?
questions.fact: Mapmakers are called cartographers.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies the ocean called?
questions.fact: Oceanographers study waves, currents, sea life and the sea floor.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies volcanoes called?
questions.fact: Volcanologists wear heat-resistant suits to get close to lava.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies earthquakes called?
questions.fact: Seismologists use networks of instruments to find where earthquakes start.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies glaciers called?
questions.fact: Glaciologists drill ice cores to learn about Earth's past climate.

questions.q: What can ice cores drilled from glaciers tell scientists?
choices: What Earth's air and climate were like long ago
questions.fact: Bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice hold samples of air from about 800,000 years ago.

questions.q: How can tree rings tell us about past weather?
choices: Wide rings mean good growing years, thin rings mean hard years
They show the temperature in numbers
questions.fact: The study of tree rings is called dendrochronology.

questions.q: What are the four main parts of the water cycle?
questions.fact: The same water has been cycling around Earth for billions of years.

questions.q: What is water that soaks into the ground called?
questions.fact: Sandy ground lets water soak in quickly, while clay slows it down.

questions.q: What is a natural place where groundwater flows out onto the surface?
questions.fact: Some springs are hot because the water is heated deep underground.

questions.q: What makes a cloud turn dark gray before rain?
choices: It is so thick with water drops that sunlight cannot get through
questions.fact: Thin clouds look white because light passes through and scatters.

questions.q: Why does it often rain more on one side of a mountain range?
choices: Air rises over the mountains, cools and drops its rain
The other side has no clouds ever
questions.fact: The dry side behind the mountains is called a rain shadow.

questions.q: What is a rain shadow?
choices: A dry area on the far side of mountains
A shadow made by rain clouds
questions.fact: The Atacama Desert and Death Valley are both in rain shadows.

questions.q: Which kind of cloud looks like a flying saucer and forms near mountains?
questions.fact: People have mistaken lenticular clouds for UFOs.

questions.q: What is the rumbling sound that follows lightning called?
questions.fact: Thunder can be heard up to about 15 kilometers from the lightning.

questions.q: What is a waterspout?
questions.fact: Waterspouts often form over warm tropical seas.

questions.q: What is a dust devil?
choices: A small spinning whirlwind of dust on a hot day
A type of tornado that lasts for weeks
questions.fact: Dust devils form when the ground gets very hot and air rises in a spinning column.

questions.q: What is a huge wall of dust blown by strong winds in deserts called?
questions.fact: Haboob comes from an Arabic word meaning strong wind.

questions.q: What are the warm, dry winds that rush down the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains called?
questions.fact: Chinooks can melt snow so fast that they are nicknamed snow eaters.

questions.q: What is it called when a hurricane pushes ocean water onto land?
questions.fact: Storm surge is often the most dangerous part of a hurricane.

questions.q: Who gives hurricanes their names?
choices: The President of the United States
questions.fact: Names of very deadly hurricanes are retired and never used again.

questions.q: What is the hurricane season in the Atlantic Ocean?
choices: All year with the same chance
questions.fact: Most Atlantic hurricanes happen from August to October.

questions.q: What is the most common type of natural disaster in the world?
questions.fact: Floods affect more people around the world than any other natural disaster.

questions.q: Why is it important to have an emergency kit at home?
choices: To have water, food and supplies if a disaster hits
questions.fact: A kit should have water, food, a flashlight, batteries and first aid supplies.

questions.q: What layer of the atmosphere has the ozone layer in it?
questions.fact: The stratosphere gets warmer as you go higher because ozone soaks up ultraviolet light.

questions.q: What is the outermost layer of Earth's atmosphere, where it fades into space, called?
questions.fact: Some satellites orbit in the exosphere.

questions.q: In which layer of the atmosphere does the International Space Station orbit?
questions.fact: The thermosphere can reach over 1,500 degrees Celsius, but the air is so thin it would not feel hot.

questions.q: What are the two main gases in Earth's air?
questions.fact: Argon is the third most common gas, at about 1 percent.

questions.q: What is the air pressure at sea level like compared to the top of Mount Everest?
questions.fact: Climbers on Everest often carry bottled oxygen because each breath holds about a third as much oxygen.

questions.q: What is the scientific name for the study of Earth's physical features and processes?
questions.fact: Geo comes from the Greek word for Earth.

questions.q: Who is often called the father of modern geology?
questions.fact: In the 1700s, Hutton argued that Earth must be extremely old because rock changes so slowly.

questions.q: What do scientists use to date very old rocks?
choices: Radioactive elements that decay at known rates
questions.fact: This method is called radiometric dating.

questions.q: How long ago did the supercontinent Pangaea begin to break apart?
questions.fact: The breakup of Pangaea created the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.q: Which two continents' coastlines fit together like puzzle pieces?
questions.fact: Matching fossils on both continents also show they were once joined.

questions.q: Which continent has the most people?
questions.fact: As of 2025, more than half of all people on Earth live in Asia.

questions.q: On which continent is the Amazon rainforest?
questions.fact: The Amazon rainforest spreads across nine countries, with the largest part in Brazil.

questions.q: What is light pollution?
choices: Too much artificial light at night that hides the stars
questions.fact: Many people in cities can no longer see the Milky Way because of light pollution.

questions.q: What is the main cause of the seasons being colder at the poles?
choices: They are farther from the Sun
Sunlight hits them at a low angle
questions.fact: Low-angle sunlight spreads its energy over a bigger area, so it heats less.

questions.q: What is the line around the Arctic where the Sun does not set on the summer solstice?
questions.fact: North of the Arctic Circle, there is at least one full day of darkness in winter.

questions.q: What is the name for the green flash that sometimes appears just as the Sun sets over the sea?
questions.fact: It happens because the atmosphere bends green light slightly more than red.

questions.q: What are sundogs?
choices: Bright spots beside the Sun caused by ice crystals
Dogs that sleep in the sun
questions.fact: Sundogs often appear on cold days when thin, icy clouds are in the sky.

questions.q: What is a halo around the Sun or Moon caused by?
questions.fact: A halo often appears when cirrus clouds are in the sky.

questions.q: What does the rhyme red sky at night, sailors' delight usually predict?
questions.fact: A red sunset often means dry air to the west, where weather usually comes from in the middle latitudes.

questions.q: What do we call a region that gets less than about 25 centimeters of rain a year?
questions.fact: Some desert plants can survive for years waiting for the next rain.

questions.q: How do cactus plants survive in the desert?
choices: They store water in their thick stems
questions.fact: Some cactuses have roots that spread out wide just under the surface to catch rain quickly.

questions.q: What is a coral reef's biggest threat as oceans warm?
choices: Too much sunlight on the beach
questions.fact: The Great Barrier Reef has had several mass bleaching events in recent years.

questions.q: What do mangrove forests do for coasts?
choices: Protect them from storms and erosion
questions.fact: Mangrove trees grow in salty water with roots that stick up above the mud.

questions.q: What gas do oceans absorb a lot of, making them more acidic?
questions.fact: Ocean acidification makes it harder for corals and shellfish to build their shells.

questions.q: What fraction of the oxygen we breathe is estimated to come from the ocean?
questions.fact: Tiny ocean plants called phytoplankton make much of this oxygen.

questions.q: What does a national park protect?
questions.fact: Yellowstone, created in 1872, is often called the world's first national park.

questions.q: What is the name of the rock layer under the crust that flows very slowly, like thick putty?
questions.fact: The tectonic plates slide around on top of this soft layer.

questions.q: What kind of seismic waves cannot travel through liquid?
questions.fact: Because S waves do not pass through the outer core, scientists learned it must be liquid.

questions.q: Which earthquake waves arrive first at a seismometer?
questions.fact: P stands for primary because these waves are the fastest.

questions.q: What do we call a crack in Earth's crust where rocks have moved?
questions.fact: Earthquakes happen when rocks along a fault suddenly slip.

questions.q: What is a deep, narrow valley on the ocean floor where one plate sinks under another called?
questions.fact: The sinking of one plate under another is called subduction.

questions.q: What is it called when one tectonic plate slides beneath another?
questions.fact: Subduction zones cause some of the most powerful earthquakes and volcanoes.

questions.q: What is an underwater mountain that does not reach the surface called?
questions.fact: There are thought to be tens of thousands of seamounts in the oceans.

questions.q: What are the wide, flat parts of the deep ocean floor called?
questions.fact: Abyssal plains are among the flattest places on Earth.

questions.q: What is the shallow, gently sloping edge of a continent under the sea called?
questions.fact: Most of the world's fishing happens over continental shelves.

questions.q: How does new ocean floor form?
choices: Magma rises at mid-ocean ridges and cools
questions.fact: This process is called seafloor spreading.

questions.q: What type of volcano is tall and cone-shaped, built from layers of lava and ash?
questions.fact: Mount Fuji and Mount St. Helens are stratovolcanoes.

questions.q: What is the smallest and simplest type of volcano, made of piled-up bits of lava?
questions.fact: Paricutin in Mexico grew from a cornfield in 1943 as a cinder cone.

questions.q: What is a vent in the ground that lets out volcanic gases and steam?
questions.fact: Some fumaroles leave behind yellow crystals of sulfur.

questions.q: What is the hard, ropy kind of lava from Hawaii called?
questions.fact: The rough, jagged kind is called aa, and both names come from the Hawaiian language.

questions.q: Which gas do volcanoes give off the most of?
questions.fact: Volcanoes also give off carbon dioxide and sulfur gases.

questions.q: How can scientists sometimes predict a volcanic eruption?
choices: By watching for small earthquakes and ground swelling
They can always predict the exact day
questions.fact: Volcano monitors also measure gases coming out of the ground.

questions.q: What do we call the remains of a dead plant or animal that has turned to stone?
questions.fact: In petrified wood, minerals slowly replaced the wood, keeping its shape.

questions.q: What is coal made from?
choices: Ancient plants buried and squeezed for millions of years
questions.fact: Much of the world's coal formed from swamp forests about 300 million years ago.

questions.q: How do plant roots help break apart rocks?
choices: They grow into cracks and push them wider
questions.fact: This is a kind of weathering.

questions.q: How does freezing water break rocks?
choices: Water in cracks expands when it freezes
questions.fact: This is called frost wedging, and it also makes potholes in roads.

questions.q: What is the slow downhill creep of soil caused by gravity called?
questions.fact: You can spot soil creep where fences and trees on a hillside lean downhill.

questions.q: Which is heavier, a cubic meter of dry air or a cubic meter of moist air at the same temperature?
questions.fact: Water vapor molecules are lighter than the nitrogen and oxygen molecules they replace.

questions.q: What is the boundary between two air masses called?
questions.fact: Weather often changes quickly when a front passes.

questions.q: What is a warm front?
choices: Warm air sliding up over colder air
questions.fact: Warm fronts often bring long, steady rain.

questions.q: What are the curving lines on a weather map that connect places with equal air pressure called?
questions.fact: When isobars are close together, the wind is strong.

questions.q: What do weather balloons carry into the sky?
choices: Instruments that measure temperature, humidity and wind
questions.fact: Weather balloons are launched around the world twice a day.

questions.q: Which weather satellites stay above one spot on Earth to watch storms?
questions.fact: They orbit about 36,000 kilometers above the equator.

questions.q: What is the cloud type that brings steady rain or snow and is dark and thick?
questions.fact: Nimbus comes from the Latin word for rain cloud.

questions.q: What are the anvil-shaped tops of thunderstorm clouds caused by?
choices: The storm cloud hitting the top of the troposphere and spreading out
Wind blowing them flat from the ground
questions.fact: The rising air cannot easily push into the warmer stratosphere above.

questions.q: What is graupel?
choices: Soft, small pellets of snow and ice
questions.fact: Graupel forms when supercooled water droplets freeze onto snowflakes.

questions.q: What is freezing rain?
choices: Rain that freezes when it hits cold surfaces
questions.fact: Freezing rain can coat roads, trees and power lines in a thick layer of ice.

questions.q: What causes the seasons to be opposite in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
choices: The Sun moves north and south
Earth's tilt points one hemisphere toward the Sun while the other points away
questions.fact: In December, the Southern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun.

questions.q: What is the main reason it is hotter at the equator than at the poles?
choices: The equator is closer to the Sun's core
Sunlight hits the equator more directly
questions.fact: The same sunlight spread over a larger area at the poles gives less heat.

questions.q: What are thick layers of mud and sand at the bottom of lakes and oceans that build up over time called?
questions.fact: Layers of sediment can hold pollen and tiny shells that reveal past climates.

questions.q: What is the process that turns loose sediment into solid rock?
questions.fact: Minerals in water act like glue to cement the grains together.

questions.q: What metamorphic rock forms when sandstone is heated and squeezed?
questions.fact: Quartzite is very hard and resists weathering.

questions.q: What gives some rocks layers or bands of different colors?
choices: Different materials deposited at different times
questions.fact: Places like the Grand Canyon show millions of years of history in their colored layers.

questions.q: Why do some rocks fizz when a drop of acid touches them?
questions.fact: Geologists use this test to identify limestone and marble.

questions.q: What is the streak test used to identify minerals?
choices: Rubbing a mineral on tile to see the color of its powder
questions.fact: Pyrite looks gold but leaves a greenish black streak.
